fundamentals.title: Similarity Solutions of Shock Formation for First-Order Strictly Hyperbolic Systems
fundamentals.abstract: Shocks due to hyperbolic partial differential equations (PDEs) appear throughout mathematics and science. The canonical example is shock formation in the inviscid Burgers equation [Formula: see text]. Previous studies have shown that when shocks form for the inviscid Burgers equation, for positions and times close to the shock singularity, the dynamics are locally self-similar and universal, i.e., dynamics are equivalent regardless of the initial conditions. In this paper, we show that, in fact, shock formation is self-similar and universal for general first-order strictly hyperbolic PDEs in one spatial dimension, and the self-similarity is like that of the inviscid Burgers equation. An analytical formula is derived for the self-similar universal solution. Reproducibility of computational results. This paper has been awarded the “SIAM Reproducibility Badge: Code and data available” as a recognition that the authors have followed reproducibility principles valued by SIREV and the scientific computing community. Code and data that allow readers to reproduce the results in this paper are available at https://doi.org/10.34770/6vgh-br25 and in the supplementary materials ( M180373_SM.zip [25.7MB]). fundamentals.title: Named Reactions under Mechanochemical Conditions: A Critical Survey
fundamentals.abstract: Mechanochemistry has progressed from a niche interest to a core method for solvent-free synthesis, providing sustainable and mechanistically unique alternatives to traditional solution-based chemistry. When controlled impact, shear, or vibrational energy is applied under solvent-free or solvent-lean conditions, reactions are promoted within dynamically renewed interfacial regions, revealing new patterns of selectivity, energy efficiency, and process design. This review surveys the historical development, fundamental principles, and analytical frameworks of mechanochemistry, together with an extensive compilation of named organic reactions conducted under mechanochemical conditions. By comparing mechanochemical reactions with their solution-phase counterparts, this review clarifies how stress-induced activation, microsolvation (η control), and auxiliary-mediated interfaces influence reaction kinetics, selectivity, and scalability. Emerging platforms, such as twin-screw extrusion (TSE), resonant acoustic mixing (RAM), and bead mills, extend these advantages toward scale-up and, in the case of TSE, continuous manufacturing, bridging laboratory-scale discoveries and industrial applications. Mechanochemistry functions both as a practical enabling platform and as a conceptual framework for Green Chemistry, embracing atom economy, solvent reduction, and operational safety within a unified solid-state synthetic framework.

fundamentals.title: On a conjecture of Almgren: area-minimizing submanifolds with fractal singular sets
fundamentals.abstract: We construct area-minimizing submanifolds with fractal singular sets on compact Riemannian manifolds. Thus, we settle a conjecture of Almgren, and our answer is sharp dimension-wise. Furthermore, we can prescribe arbitrarily the strata in the Almgren stratification of the singular sets of our area-minimizing submanifolds, and our results hold in the category of integral currents, mod v currents and stable stationary varifolds.

fundamentals.title: Linear scaling reveals low-dimensional structure in observable microbial dynamics
fundamentals.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
fundamentals.abstract: Microbial communities often exhibit apparently complex dynamics driven by myriad interactions among community members and with their environments. Yet, practical modeling and control are often based on a limited number of observables, raising fundamental questions: are these observed dynamics low-dimensional? If so, how does the low dimensionality enable predictions with limited information? Here, we report an emergent simplicity that the temporal dynamics of observable microbial populations can be captured by low-dimensional representations. Using variational autoencoders, we define a critical latent dimension ( E c ) that operationally quantifies the smallest latent dimension required for high-fidelity reconstruction of observable microbial dynamics under a specified criterion. Despite the complexity of unobserved background dynamics, we find E c to be drastically lower than the community’s apparent degrees of freedom. E c scales linearly with the number of observables, providing an empirical principle for determining representation complexity. This principle holds across simulations of pairwise interacting communities, consumer–resource dynamics, spatially distributed microbial patches, and plasmid transfer, experiments with engineered and environment-derived communities, and human microbiomes. Our findings establish a scaling law for microbial community dynamics and demonstrate that low-dimensional representations of observable dynamics retain information useful for selected prediction tasks without direct measurement of the complete community.

fundamentals.title: Foiling Black Hole Foils: Revealing Horizon Alternatives with Baryonic Atmospheres
fundamentals.abstract: Event horizons are a defining feature of black holes. Consequently, there have been many efforts to probe their existence in astrophysical black hole candidates, spanning 10 orders of magnitude in mass. Nevertheless, horizons remain an obstacle to unifying general relativity and quantum mechanics, most sharply presented by the information paradox. This has motivated a proliferation of horizonless alternatives (black hole foils) that avoid event horizons and are therefore presumably benign. We explore the fate of accreting material in the context of spherically symmetric horizonless compact objects in the steady state regime. We find that for typical accreting astronomical targets, foils can develop an optically thick, convectively stable baryonic atmosphere, immediately implying the creation of an emitting photosphere at modest redshift even when the surface redshift is extreme. The emergent photosphere luminosity is driven toward the accretion powered equilibrium value and is only weakly sensitive to the foil redshift. Moreover, local gas–surface interaction provides a microphysical lower bound on the effective base temperature, insulating the atmosphere from arbitrarily cold foils. The unknown properties of the foil enter only through local boundary conditions controlling baryon processing and thermal coupling at the surface, making the solutions broadly applicable to horizonless alternatives that do not invoke significant additional nonlocal interactions. Thus, under minimal assumptions (GR exterior and local surface interactions), spherically symmetric horizonless foils in accreting systems are generically observationally exposed: the absence of a thermal photosphere directly constrains or rules out broad classes of such models.

fundamentals.title: Diffusion Models for Small-Molecule Design
fundamentals.abstract: Diffusion models (DMs) have emerged as a class of generative models for controllable small-molecule design in drug discovery capable of progressively transforming noisy or partially specified molecular states into candidate structures under structural, geometric, and property constraints. This Review provides a comprehensive overview of the methodological foundations and representative applications of diffusion-based molecular generation, emphasizing the alignment among molecular representations, generative dynamics, controllable design, and evaluation and validation. Particular attention is given to recent advances in property- and structure-guided generation, target-aware and fragment-based design, multiobjective optimization, and synthesis-aware generation. We also discuss the roles of data sets, computational evaluation, and prospective experiments in assessing the chemical and biological relevance of generated molecules. By organizing these developments within a unified conceptual framework, we provide computational chemists and drug discovery researchers with a structured roadmap that balances the mathematical rigor with chemical intuition. Throughout, we highlight current methodological limitations and unresolved challenges and conclude with future directions toward chemically credible and experimentally grounded molecular design. To facilitate navigation of this rapidly evolving field, we introduce an interactive companion platform (https://diffsmd.scbdd.com) that provides a curated, continuously updated repository of model architectures and visualizations.

fundamentals.title: Bright Galaxies at Cosmic Dawn: A Cloud-Scale Star Formation Model Unifying Variable SFE, IMFs, and Stochasticity
fundamentals.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
fundamentals.abstract: To investigate the origins of the high abundance of UV-bright galaxies at z > 10, we present a new semi-analytic model that bridges the gap between small-scale star formation physics and large-scale galaxy evolution by explicitly tracking discrete star-forming clouds within smoothly evolving dark matter potentials. Unlike conventional semi-analytic models, our approach naturally captures the stochasticity of star formation, allowing us to isolate how cloud properties, star formation efficiencies (SFEs), and stellar initial mass functions (IMFs) shape the star-formation burstiness of early galaxies. Clouds are drawn sequentially from a cloud mass distribution, assigned an SFE and IMF depending on cloud mass, metallicity, and redshift, and evolve under the influence of short-timescale stellar feedback. We identify three distinct star formation regimes arising from the interplay between cloud masses, densities, and feedback timescales: a stochastic, feedback-limited regime in low-mass halos with long quiescent phases; a bursty regime regulated by the cloud mass distribution; and a smooth, continuous regime in massive halos. Our fiducial model adopts a dynamic IMF, an SFE linked to cloud properties and the IMF, and massive, moderately dense clouds. Varying assumptions reveals that top-heavy IMFs and enhanced SFEs in massive clouds amplify burstiness, while altering the upper cloud mass or density normalisation is secondary. Among model ingredients, the IMF most strongly impacts the UV luminosity function (LF), while switching to a constant SFE boosts the faint end, and reducing the maximum cloud mass decreases the bright end. These results demonstrate that cloud-scale physics critically shape early galaxy UV luminosity distributions.

fundamentals.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals molecular organization of human and nonhuman primate basal ganglia
fundamentals.abstract: The basal ganglia (BG) are interconnected subcortical nuclei with a complex topographical organization that orchestrate goal-directed behaviors and are implicated in neurodegenerative movement disorders. We generated a cellular-resolution spatial transcriptomics atlas of the BG in human, rhesus macaque, and common marmoset, sampling over one million cells in each species. By integrating spatial data with a cross-species consensus single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) cell-type taxonomy, this atlas reveals principles of molecular organization within and across structures. Extensive spatial sampling across the rostral-caudal axis illuminates complex, yet highly stereotyped, multi-axis gene expression gradients superimposed onto discrete compartments of the striatum. Additionally, we identify core-shell organization of the internal globus pallidus. This unified, cross-species spatial transcriptomics atlas will be a foundational resource for characterizing the molecular and functional organization of the BG and their roles in health and disease.

fundamentals.title: The commutativity problem for effective varieties of formal series, and applications
fundamentals.abstract: A formal series in noncommuting variables Σ over the rationals is a mapping Σ * → Q from the free monoid generated by Σ to the rationals. We say that it is commutative if the output does not depend on the order of the symbols in the input. The commutativity problem for a class of series takes as input a (finite presentation of) a series from the class and amounts to establishing whether it is commutative. This is a very natural, albeit nontrivial problem, which has not been considered before from an algorithmic perspective. We show that commutativity is decidable for all classes of series that constitute a so-called effective prevariety , a notion generalising Reutenauer’s varieties of formal series. For example, the class of rational series , introduced by Schützenberger in the 1960’s, is well-known to be an effective (pre)variety, and thus commutativity is decidable for it. In order to showcase the applicability of our result, we consider classes of formal series generalising the rational ones. We consider polynomial automata , shuffle automata , and infiltration automata , and we show that each of these models recognises an effective prevariety of formal series. Consequently, their commutativity problem is decidable, which is a novel result. We find it remarkable that commutativity can be decided in a uniform way for such disparate computation models. Finally, we present applications of commutativity outside the theory of formal series. We show that we can decide solvability in sequences and in power series for restricted classes of algebraic difference and differential equations, for which such problems are undecidable in full generality. Thanks to this, we can prove that the syntaxes of multivariate polynomial recursive sequences and of constructible…

fundamentals.title: Electric Field Catalysis and the Metabolic Origin of Life
fundamentals.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
fundamentals.abstract: Metabolic theories for the origin of life postulate that chemical reaction networks emerged spontaneously from geochemistry and grew more complex due to positive feedback effects in catalysis. However, experimentally establishing protometabolic networks has proven challenging. In this Perspective, we make the case for electric field catalysis at charged aqueous interfaces as a crucial overlooked element for initiating protometabolic networks, an initial constraint that foreshadows the eventual takeover of electrostatic catalysis by enzymes. We first overview types of positive feedback relevant to the early evolution of metabolism, the theory of electric field catalysis, and its dominant role in enzyme catalysis. We then examine recent experiments and calculations highlighting the ability of external electric fields to enable nonenzymatic analogues of challenging metabolic reactions in micro- to millisecond reaction times. An underexplored mode of small molecule catalysis (reorientation catalysis) that can only operate in external electric fields is proposed to make positive feedback within prebiotic reaction networks more achievable. By embodying electrostatic catalysis, compartmentalization, and ion concentration gradients, charged aqueous interfaces prepattern three fundamental features of biology, making them a preferred environment for a metabolic origin of life. Making robust progress on the origin of life may surprisingly require exploring the nascent area of electric field-mediated chemistry at aqueous interfaces. Life does not use electric fields to catalyze its metabolic network by accident.

fundamentals.title: Substitutional Quantification and Arithmetical Truth
fundamentals.abstract: In the mid‐20th century, there was a debate about whether the quantifiers in first‐order logic should be understood objectually or substitutionally. This debate typically focused on ontology and assumed that we could use only one of these two types of quantification. After Kripke and others influentially argued that the two kinds of quantification were logically equivalent, defenses of substitutional quantification were rare. Following Gottlieb and Field, I argue that Kripke was wrong and that substitutional consequence is language‐bound and non‐compact. While of no help with ontology, I also argue that so‐understood, substitutional quantification can be applied to help explain our grasp of a determinate notion of arithmetical truth. To argue for this, I give an account of the metasemantics of the substitutional quantifiers and prove that adding a single, very natural, mixed axiom to weak theories of arithmetic results in a categorical theory. This approach promises to explain arithmetical truth on a less controversial basis than appeals to either second‐order logic or the omega rule, thus making progress on the project of explaining our grasp of arithmetic in a naturalistically acceptable fashion.

fundamentals.title: Tidal Deformation and Strain Accumulation of Solid Compact Stars
fundamentals.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
fundamentals.abstract: The tidal deformability of compact stars encodes the equation of state of dense matter, and gravitational-wave observations such as GW170817 have begun to constrain it under the assumption of a fluid interior. Yet whether the interior of pulsar-like compact stars is fluid or solid remains largely untested, despite the distinct tidal responses the two states predict. In this work, based on the strangeon-star model, we develop a framework for modeling tidal deformation in solid compact stars. Adopting a shear modulus of μ = 1034 erg cm−3, we find a relative difference of approximately 30 % in tidal deformability between solid and fluid strangeon stars of 1.4 M⊙, corresponding to a ~10 % deviation from the universal I–Love relation. We further model the accumulation of internal strain during binary inspiral and find that it peaks near the stellar center. When the gravitational-wave frequency reaches several hundred Hz, the strain in a large fraction of the stellar volume exceeds the adopted threshold σ = 10−3, and the elastic energy stored in the threshold-exceeding region reaches ~1046 erg at these frequencies. A solid-to-fluid transition would alter the tidal response and could imprint on the waveform and phase of the emitted gravitational radiation. Combined with the precursor electromagnetic emission, these gravitational-wave signatures offer a multi-messenger avenue to test the solid nature of pulsar-like compact stars.

fundamentals.title: Solving the Dual Puzzles of Collective Harm
fundamentals.abstract: Suppose some uncoordinated group of agents causes tremendous harm, but none of the individuals could have meaningfully changed this result by acting differently. These “collective harm” cases have been the subject of extended philosophical discussion, but this paper argues that there are really two different, if connected, puzzles presented by such cases: (1) a puzzle about how to characterize the moral injury to those who suffer this harm (the “wrongness puzzle”) and (2) a puzzle about why agents may do something wrong in participating in producing this harm (the “participation puzzle”). This paper elaborates these puzzles, defends the idea that they are different from each other, and offers solutions to them both. The core idea is that an application of the distinction between ideal and nonideal theory can shed light on both puzzles; the injury experienced by the victims of collective harm is to be understood in terms of the shortfall they suffer from how they would fare if ideal circumstances obtained, and participation in collective harm is wrong when it involves reasoning that fails to appropriately apply ideal moral rules to nonideal situations.

fundamentals.title: A Log-Uniform Initial Magnetic Field Distribution Explains Pulsar and Magnetar Populations through Magnetic Inclination Alignment
fundamentals.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
fundamentals.abstract: The origin of the gap in the observed magnetic field distribution between pulsars and magnetars raises a challenge to understanding these populations within a unified framework. We analytically show that the gap can be naturally explained by the alignment of the magnetic inclination angle between the magnetic and spin axes. Based on coupled evolution of spin-down and magnetic inclination angle in the plasma-filled magnetosphere, the alignment timescale follows τα∝B−2. Thus, strongly magnetized neutron stars including high-B pulsars and magnetars align more rapidly than pulsars with 1012 G, reducing their beaming fraction and thereby suppressing their observed numbers. However, magnetars are primarily identified through X-ray activity and are therefore relatively less affected by beaming. Taking into account both beaming fraction and luminosity corrections, we reconstruct the initial magnetic field distribution from the observed distribution. We show that pulsars and magnetars do not dictate intrinsically distinct initial distributions, but can instead be understood within a single continuous initial magnetic field distribution, such as a log-uniform distribution.

fundamentals.title: On the Orbital Evolution of Giant-planet Pair Embedded in a Gaseous Disk. III. Simultaneous Gas Accretion and the Final Mass Ratio
fundamentals.abstract: Recent exoplanet surveys reveal a systematic trend in the mass ratios of giant-planet pairs (>30 M ⊕ ). Although the M outer / M inner is broadly centered near unity, it exhibits a dependence on orbital separation. Compact pairs tend to have comparable masses, whereas widely separated pairs show outer-heavy configurations. To investigate the origin of this trend, we perform 2D hydrodynamic simulations that couple gas accretion and orbital migration of two giant planet embryos with initial masses of 15−30 M ⊕ . We explore the effects of disk viscosity, surface density slope, and initial mass ratio on the coupled evolution of planetary growth and migration. We find that convergent migration drives the planets to open a common gap, restructuring the gas flow. This configuration induces asymmetric accretion, in which the inner planet becomes starved as gap clearing suppresses its gas supply, while the outer planet continues to accrete from the high-density region at the outer gap edge. Consequently, the system naturally evolves toward mass-ratio convergence, and in many cases produces an inversion of the initial core-mass hierarchy. We further show that migration outcomes are highly sensitive to initial conditions. Systems with initially more massive inner cores tend to diverge, whereas steeper surface density profiles and more massive outer cores favor convergent migration and subsequent resonance capture. Overall, our results identify common-gap-driven asymmetric accretion as a unified mechanism linking orbital architecture, resonant capture, and the observed mass-ratio demographics of giant planet pairs.

fundamentals.title: A Unified Reactivity Scale Predicts Nonenzymatic Phosphoryl Transfer and Nucleophilic Catalysis in Water
fundamentals.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
fundamentals.abstract: The transfer of phosphoryl groups plays a central role in biochemical energy metabolism. Understanding how such reactions could have occurred before the emergence of enzymes is thus crucial for elucidating the chemical foundations of life. Although the factors governing the mechanisms of phosphoryl transfer in water are well understood, predicting whether a given nucleophile and phosphorylating agent will undergo productive phosphoryl transfer rather than hydrolysis remains difficult, thereby hindering the rational exploration of nonenzymatic phosphorylation reactions. Herein, we establish a quantitative reactivity scale that predicts absolute rate constants for nonenzymatic phosphoryl transfer reactions in water based on a linear free-energy relationship (LFER). Using high-throughput kinetics, we measured 11,520 phosphoryl transfer reactions for 145 unique combinations of nucleophiles and phosphorylating agents under varying reaction conditions. Mechanism-specific rate constants extracted from this data for 102 substrate pairs, together with values scraped from the literature, enabled us to parametrize an LFER that places 34 phosphorylating agents and 45 nucleophiles on a unified quantitative reactivity scale, enabling predictions across 14 orders of magnitude in reactivity. Finally, we show that the empirically derived reactivity parameters can be used to predict optimal nucleophilic catalysts by balancing the competing steps in catalytic turnover, as experimentally validated for the reaction of monoamidophosphate with pyridines. For phosphorylating agents of intermediate electrophilicity such as ATP, imidazole is predicted to be the optimal catalyst, offering a kinetic rationale for the prevalence of histidine residues in enzymatic phosphoryl transfer. food.title: Impact of arsenic exposure on the gut-microbiota-liver axis in poultry
food.abstract: Arsenic (As), a priority hazardous substance widely distributed in nature, endangers poultry health and food safety. The gut‑microbiota‑liver axis forms a bidirectional regulatory network, with the intestine acting as the main absorption site and the liver as the key metabolic‑detoxification organ for As. This review summarizes arsenic‑induced toxic injuries to this axis in poultry. In the intestine, As impairs mucosal barrier function, triggers epithelial cell death via NF‑κB‑NLRP3 inflammasome activation, and causes leaky‑gut syndrome. It also disturbs gut microbiota homeostasis, lowering beneficial butyrate‑producing bacteria and impairing short‑chain‑fatty‑acid synthesis. In the liver, As disrupts energy metabolism, provokes severe oxidative stress, and triggers multiple forms of programmed cell death, including ferroptosis and PANoptosis. Gut-derived lipopolysaccharide translocates to the liver via the portal circulation, amplifying hepatic inflammation, which in turn causes altered bile acid metabolism and reduced short-chain fatty acid production, thereby triggering gut microbiota dysbiosis and forming a self-reinforcing vicious cycle. Potential interventions including probiotics, polysaccharides, selenium and vitamin E are discussed to counteract arsenic toxicity. This work provides theoretical support for arsenic risk control in poultry farming.

food.title: Prevalence and Levels of Mycotoxins in Poultry Feed and Ingredients: A Global Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
food.abstract: Mycotoxins are a global concern due to their widespread occurrence throughout the food chain and their potential risks to human and animal health. This study investigated the global prevalence and concentrations of mycotoxins in poultry feed and its components, assessing their potential health implication. Following the PRISMA methodology, 78 articles were included, with data processed (outlier removal) and analysed using STATA®. Globally, fumonisins B1 (FB1) and B2 (FB2) were the most prevalent (70% and 68%), with concentrations of 1,159 µg kg –1 and 164 µg kg –1 , respectively. The prevalence of aflatoxins (AFs), zearalenone (ZEN), deoxynivalenol (DON), ochratoxins (OTs), T-2/HT-2 toxins, emerging (overall pooled value of fusaric acid (FUS), enniatins (ENNs), apicidin (API), alternariol (AOH), nivalenol (NIV), beauvericin (BEA), patulin (PAT), moniliformin (MON), diacetoxyscirpenol (DAS), ergot alkaloids (EA), kojic acid (KA), tenuazonic acid (TeA), scirpentriol (SCIRP), cyclopiazonic acid (CPA), citrinin (CIT), fusarenon-X (FUS-X), T-2 triol/tetraol, and sterigmatocystin (STG)), and masked/modified mycotoxins (overall pooled value of deoxynivalenol-3-glucoside (D3G), 3-acetyl-deoxynivalenol (3-Ac-DON), and 15-acetyl-deoxynivalenol (15-Ac-DON)) appeared as 64%, 59%, 46%, 41%, 45%, 53% and 37%, with corresponding concentrations of 25.2, 204, 522, 36.6, 154, 15.8 and 35.0 µg kg –1 , respectively. Cotton, barley, sunflower, and maize meals showed high concentrations of multiple mycotoxins ( viz ., ZEN, FBs, and DON). Except for the AFs, all concentrations were below the Maximum Limits (MLs)/Guidance Values (GVs) established by the European Commission (EC 2002; EC 2006). food.title: Interactive effects of dietary total sulfur amino acids and crude protein on productive performance in laying hens: A meta-analysis
food.abstract: Dietary total sulfur amino acids (TSAA) play essential roles in egg protein synthesis and various metabolic functions in laying hens, underscoring the importance of accurate estimation of TSAA requirements, particularly when formulating low-CP diets. A previous meta-analysis in broiler chickens revealed that optimal TSAA levels increase as dietary CP levels decrease; however, quantitative information regarding this interactive effect across different phases of the prolonged laying cycle remains limited in laying hens. Therefore, the current meta-analysis aimed to determine the interactive relationship between dietary CP and digestible TSAA levels for optimizing productive performance in laying hens across laying phases. A total of 28 studies published between 2010 and 2026 were analyzed using a mixed model with study as a random effect and observations weighted by the number of replicates. Productive performance variables included hen-d egg production (HEP), egg weight (EW), egg mass (EM), average daily feed intake (ADFI), and feed conversion ratio (FCR). The quadratic model with the product of digestible TSAA and total CP (TSAA × CP) as a single predictor, which was developed in our previous meta-analysis for broiler chickens, was fitted separately in different laying phases. Models were conservatively retained only when the intercept and regression coefficients were all significant (P < 0.05). Accordingly, models were retained for ADFI and FCR in phase 1 (early-phase), for HEP, EM, and ADFI in phase 2 (mid-phase), and for all variables in the overall dataset. However, no significant models were identified in phase 3 (late-phase), possibly due to the limited number of observations and between-study heterogeneity. food.title: Epidemiology, co-infection and risk factors of major poultry respiratory pathogens in North Africa: a narrative review (2000-2025)
food.abstract: Background Poultry respiratory diseases are a major threat to food security, farmer livelihoods, and public health in North Africa. The region comprises Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Egypt, Libya, and Mauritania, where commercial and backyard poultry systems are highly susceptible to respiratory pathogens. Disease emergence and spread are facilitated by major migratory bird flyways, live bird markets, cross-border poultry trade, limited surveillance and diagnostic capacity in several countries. Methods A narrative review of peer-reviewed literature published between January 2000 and December 2025 was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and ScienceDirect. Search terms included “poultry respiratory disease,” “avian influenza,” “Newcastle disease,” “infectious bronchitis,” “avian metapneumovirus,” “Mycoplasma gallisepticum,” “co-infection,” “epidemiology,” and the names of the six North African countries. Original prevalence, surveillance, molecular, and epidemiological studies were included, while grey literature and conference abstracts were excluded. FAO and WOAH reports supplemented data for Mauritania and Libya. Of 561 records identified, 273 met the inclusion criteria. Results Newcastle disease virus (NDV) and infectious bronchitis virus (IBV) are enzootic throughout North Africa, with the highest reported prevalence in Algeria (NDV: 82.7%; IBV: 78.2%) values are estimates from individual studies rather than nationally representative prevalence estimates. Low-pathogenic avian influenza H9N2 is endemic across all six countries, while highly pathogenic H5N1 has been reported in Egypt, Libya, Algeria, and Mauritania, and H5N8 in Egypt and Algeria. Avian metapneumovirus subtype B circulates in Morocco, Algeria, and Tunisia, with seroprevalence…

food.title: Ultrasound as a Multifunctional Physical Platform for Whole‐Grape Valorization: From Field Management to Green Extraction, Quality Modulation, and Intelligent Scale‐Up
food.journal: Comprehensive Reviews in Food Science and Food Safety
food.abstract: The grape and wine industry faces prolonged barrel aging, microbial spoilage, protein haze, chemical additives, and inefficient by-product valorization. These challenges motivate nonthermal technologies that reduce chemical inputs. Ultrasound operates in two mechanistically distinct regimes: sensing, based on acoustic propagation, reflection, and echo detection, and processing, driven mainly by acoustic cavitation and its physical and chemical effects, including microjets, shock waves, localized hotspots, and reactive radicals. These complementary modes provide a versatile physical platform. This review covers ultrasound across the grape-wine continuum: acoustic imaging for precision viticulture; postharvest preservation with green activated water; green extraction enhanced by natural deep eutectic solvents; grape protein modification for ingredient assembly; modulation of wine color, aroma, and colloidal stability; selected aging-associated reactions involving 1-hydroxyethyl radicals; selective microbial inactivation and fermentation modulation; and scale-up based on energy characterization, continuous-flow reactors, and data-driven modeling. Current evidence indicates that ultrasound is evolving from an empirically optimized unit operation toward a mechanistically informed and quantitatively characterized physical-field platform. Reported effects include accelerated aging-related transformations, modified protein structure and stability, and selective microbial responses, although they depend on treatment conditions and matrix properties. Absorbed energy density supports quantitative comparison of treatments, but reliable scale-up also requires acoustic-field distribution, residence time, temperature, and reactor geometry. Future progress will require standardized…

food.title: Plasma-Based Technologies for Aquatic Product Preservation: Balancing Microbial Control and Oxidative Deterioration
food.abstract: : Background Aquatic products are highly nutritious but are particularly susceptible to microbial contamination, lipid oxidation, and protein degradation during postharvest handling and storage, posing challenges to food safety, quality preservation, and sustainable cold-chain logistics. Atmospheric cold plasma (ACP) and plasma-activated liquids (PALs), particularly plasma-activated water (PAW), have emerged as promising non-thermal preservation technologies because they generate reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS) capable of inactivating microorganisms while minimizing thermal damage. Scope and approach This review critically summarizes recent advances in the application of ACP and PALs for aquatic product preservation, with particular emphasis on the mechanisms underlying microbial inactivation and the complex interactions among microorganisms, proteins, lipids, and plasma-generated reactive species. Rather than considering microbial safety and quality independently, this review highlights how ACP simultaneously regulates microbial growth, protein oxidation, lipid oxidation, and volatile flavor formation, thereby determining the overall preservation outcome. Key findings and conclusions Current evidence indicates that the efficacy of ACP is highly dependent on treatment intensity, plasma operating conditions, and food matrix characteristics, requiring a careful balance between effective microbial control and the prevention of excessive oxidative deterioration. The review further discusses key barriers to industrial implementation, including the lack of standardized processing protocols, insufficient dose–response characterization, limited toxicological evidence, equipment scalability, and regulatory uncertainty. Finally, future research priorities are…

food.title: Novel electron transport powers archaeal methane metabolism across varied substrates and environments
food.abstract: Methanogens are responsible for producing approximately one billion metric tons of methane each year within Earth’s anaerobic environments as a byproduct of their energy metabolism. They play a vital role in the global carbon cycle. There are three main pathways for methanogenesis: hydrogenotrophic, which uses H 2 and CO 2 to produce methane; methylotrophic, which utilizes methylated compounds like methanol and amines; and aceticlastic, which converts acetate into methane and CO 2 . Instead of substrate-level ATP production, methanogens conserve energy through a membrane-bound electron transport chain and flavin-based electron bifurcation (FBEB). Beyond the canonical modes of growth in methanogens, Methanosarcina acetivorans , a model acetotrophic methanogen, can conserve energy via direct interspecies electron transfer (DIET). Here, we review the metabolic pathways and electron transport processes involved in energy conservation during fermentative, respiratory, and DIET modes. Additionally, we discuss the role of FBEB in energy conservation in gut-associated Methanomassiliicoccus luminyensis . Finally, we discuss the potential roles of heterodisulfide reductase (Hdr) and the process of electron transfer during the reaction mechanism of electron-bifurcating HdrA2B2C2 complex in cytochrome-containing methanogens. Understanding the complex redox control mechanisms in these organisms has broader implications for sustainable energy and environmental management.

food.title: Microbial Safety of Pecans: Contamination Pathways, Postharvest Interventions, and Food Safety Applications of Pecan Shells
food.journal: Comprehensive Reviews in Food Science and Food Safety
food.abstract: Pecans are a valuable commodity in North America but have been implicated in multiple recalls, primarily linked to Salmonella contamination. Pathogenic contamination can occur at multiple points along the production chain from farm to postharvest processing. Pecans remain a food safety concern because of their association with Salmonella-related recalls and the pathogen's ability to infiltrate in-shell pecans during postharvest handling and survive for extended periods. Therefore, various thermal and nonthermal postharvest treatments exist for their decontamination. This review summarizes the routes of microbial contamination in pecans, traditional and emerging strategies employed to inactivate pathogens, as well as the potential use of pecan shell by-products for food safety. Thermal treatments, such as hot water, steam, hot air, and oil roasting, have demonstrated effective inactivation of foodborne pathogens on in-shell pecans and kernels under specific treatment conditions with minimal changes to the nuts' quality parameters. Chemical sanitizers generally provide lower reductions and are widely used to minimize or prevent cross-contamination but show limited efficacy as a decontamination step to achieve 5-log reduction. Emerging nonthermal techniques, such as intense pulsed light and cold atmospheric plasma, demonstrate potential for pathogens reduction on pecans. Lastly, pecan shells, comprising 40%-60% of the whole nut, are rich in phenolic and flavonoid compounds with antimicrobial and antioxidant properties. Recent studies highlight their potential as natural antimicrobials, functional ingredients, and active packaging components in food safety applications. Overall, this review integrates current knowledge on contamination risks, intervention strategies,…

food.title: Dietary Organosulfur‐Containing Compounds (DOSCs) as Healthy Longevity Agents: Mechanisms, Evidence, and Future Perspectives
food.journal: Comprehensive Reviews in Food Science and Food Safety
food.abstract: Aging is a complex biological process characterized by a gradual decline in physiological functions and increased risk of chronic diseases. The framework of "hallmarks of aging" provides a foundation for identifying actionable targets to delay aging and extend healthspan. Among dietary interventions, bioactive compounds may modulate aging-related pathways. Dietary organosulfur-containing compounds (DOSCs), abundant in Allium vegetables, Brassicaceae species and moringa, and other natural sources (e.g., stink and djenkol beans, shiitake mushrooms), have attracted significant attention due to their pleiotropic health-promoting properties. Historically used in traditional medicine, DOSCs are now recognized for their antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, cardioprotective, and neuroprotective activities. Our review conducts a comprehensive analysis of current knowledge on DOSCs as potential antiaging agents. We first outline their classification, dietary sources, and derivatives formed during food processing (particularly heat treatment and fermentation), highlighting how culinary practices modulate their concentrations and biological efficacy. Additionally, preclinical studies in model organisms and clinical investigations demonstrate that DOSCs can attenuate oxidative damage, improve mitochondrial function, modulate inflammatory signaling, and enhance resilience against age-related decline. Mechanistic insights suggest that DOSCs influence multiple hallmarks of aging. Despite promising findings, challenges remain regarding their bioavailability, interindividual variability, and limited long-term human data. Therefore, innovative strategies such as novel delivery systems, personalized nutrition, combination therapies with established geroprotective agents, and AI-driven…

food.title: From Printability to Product Quality in 3D and 4D Food Printing: Evidence, Comparability, and Translation
food.journal: Comprehensive Reviews in Food Science and Food Safety
food.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) and four-dimensional (4D) food printing technologies have evolved from shape-making demonstrations to digitally controlled food production. However, comparative literature remains challenging due to incomplete reporting on material preparation, rheological experimental protocols, printer configurations, and product quality measurements. Furthermore, food-related findings are often discussed alongside non-food engineering concepts, lacking a clear distinction in the weight of evidence. This review analyzes the entire production chain, from material preparation and rheological characterization to printer operation, printed product quality, and application deployment. At each stage, we examine whether reported results are supported by adequate testing conditions, controls, variability estimates, and food-related evidence. Reported rheological ranges cannot define a universal printability window, as their meaning depends on measurement and printing conditions. A printed food can only be classified as 4D food if its response is intentionally programmed during printing, activated by specific stimuli, measured over time, and repeated across different samples. Evidence regarding sensory acceptability, clinical application, hygiene, shelf life, yield, and resource utilization is far less mature than evidence regarding geometric feasibility. In summary, existing literature supports conditional material-process relationships rather than validated universal models. Integrating the information needed to interpret and reproduce these relationships by domain of evidence allows for the differentiation of findings from food validation studies from specific system observations and engineering assumptions that still require testing in edible systems.

food.title: Complications with current molecular assays that utilize DNA sequencing for analyzing species in Canned tuna: A Review
food.abstract: Canned tuna presents unique challenges for species identification using DNA analysis methods due to several factors including the severe thermal processing required for commercial sterility and the ubiquitous nature of environmental DNA (eDNA). Retorting cans of tuna at 110-121°C for extended periods fragments DNA into short, unevenly degraded pieces making DNA analysis challenging. Tuna and other fish also shed large quantities of eDNA throughout the supply chain, from ocean water, purse-seine wells, refrigerated brine, thawing systems, and factory surfaces, resulting in unavoidable adventitious DNA that can accompany the target species into the can. This review examines the industrial and regulatory factors that complicate the interpretation of DNA results from retorted tuna and the existing assays that are currently being used to identify what species are present in cans of tuna. While traditional PCR, qPCR and Next Gen sequencing methodologies are currently being used to detect species in cans of tuna, these assays are currently not being run in a manner that allows for quantification of samples. This allows for eDNA to be overestimated in cans of tuna and is unrelated to muscle meat. Consequently, the presence of multiple tuna DNA signatures in a can does not reliably indicate species substitution or fraud. Regulatory frameworks acknowledge up to 5% adventitious carry-over in processed foods, and similar thresholds are appropriate for canned tuna given the realities of fishing, handling, and processing. Overall, current DNA technologies are not best suited as proxies for determining the species composition of cooked muscle meat in canned tuna, and misinterpretation of eDNA signals carry risks of false accusations of mislabeling or fraud, rather than unintentional…

food.title: Sub-Inhibitory Plant-Derived GRAS Compounds and the Salmonella Type III Secretion System: A Critical Review and a Genotype-Informed Path Forward
food.abstract: Plant-derived compounds that are generally recognized as safe (GRAS) suppress Salmonella virulence gene expression at concentrations that do not inhibit growth. A recent comprehensive review covered this phenomenon broadly across membrane, efflux, quorum-sensing, and biofilm mechanisms. The present review takes a narrower view and examines one axis, the Type III Secretion System (T3SS) that translocates effector proteins during host-cell invasion. At growth-curve-confirmed subinhibitory concentrations, eugenol, thymol, carvacrol, and cinnamaldehyde downregulate T3SS-associated transcripts. In the most well-studied cases, this downregulation also extends to effector proteins. That evidence is summarized here and placed alongside the adjacent quorum-sensing, biofilm, and sub-MIC antibiotic literature, together with reporting gaps in PCR primer background and amplicon efficiency that limit how far some of these results can be pushed. Two questions relevant to preharvest control, with poultry production as the primary applied context, remain largely unaddressed. The first is whether the magnitude of virulence suppression varies predictably across genetically diverse Salmonella strains at two main resolutions: serovar and SNP-variation within a serovar. The second question is whether structure-guided computational screening can expand the candidate pool beyond the four essential oil constituents that dominate this review. To define potential targets for such screens, the 30 Salmonella T3SS structures currently available in the Protein Data Bank are summarized here by functional class. Answering both questions would move the field toward genomically informed, strain-specific compound selection as a precision preharvest intervention.

food.title: Sustainable 2-keto-L-gulonic acid biosynthesis via single-strain one-step fermentation
food.abstract: L-ascorbic acid (vitamin C) is an essential antioxidant molecule that maintains normal physiological functions in humans. Currently, industrial production relies primarily on a three-strain, two-step fermentation process to produce 2-keto-L-gulonic acid (2-KLG), the direct precursor of vitamin C. 2-KLG is then converted to vitamin C through chemical lactonization. However, this process is limited by prolonged fermentation cycles, poor stability of the mixed-culture system, and complex process control. In recent years, engineered single-strain platforms capable of one-step 2-KLG biosynthesis have emerged as a promising strategy for more sustainable vitamin C production. Nevertheless, the efficiency of L-sorbose-to-2-KLG conversion in this system remains low, making it a major bottleneck to further improving 2-KLG production. This review summarizes recent advances on single-strain, one-step fermentation systems using Gluconobacter oxydans as the chassis strain. It focuses on strategies including genetic tool development, metabolic engineering, and key enzyme optimization. The review aims to provide a theoretical basis and technical reference for optimizing and industrializing green biomanufacturing systems for vitamin C.

food.title: Regulatory governance and full-scale digital transformation for prediction-based food safety management: Global trends and future perspectives
food.abstract: Background The global food safety paradigm is shifting from traditional, reactive hazard control toward proactive, predictive risk management to address increasingly complex supply chain vulnerabilities. However, current digital implementations remain fragmented, creating structural bottlenecks that hinder the transition to next-generation regulatory science. Scope and approach To our knowledge, this study provides one of the first comparative critical analyses of the HACCP-based data governance frameworks of six major jurisdictions. We compare jurisdictions in which private actors play a relatively larger role in certification and implementation ('market-led': the United States, the European Union, Canada, and Japan) with those in which public institutions play a dominant role ('state-led': South Korea and China), positioned along a governance continuum in which all systems combine public and private functions, focusing on their capacity for real-time risk prediction, public-private data integration, and global interoperability. Key findings and conclusions The market-led systems examined tend to foster food safety culture but are affected by 'Data Silos' that limit actions to retrospective tracebacks. The state-led systems examined may enhance data integrity but can create a 'Data Island' paradox due to an over-reliance on automating isolated physico-chemical Critical Control Points. To overcome these limitations, we propose a conceptual framework for Full-Scale Digital Transformation (Full DX). Converging prerequisite programs, structured food safety culture assessment (e.g., Shapley-FAHP), and intentional threat mitigations (TACCP/VACCP) into an interoperable predictive network powered by ensemble machine learning could support a more resilient regulatory…

food.title: Persistent Biofilms in the Food Industry: Mechanistic Insights, Emerging Interventions, and Smart Processing Frontiers.
food.abstract: Background Biofilms are a major microbiological concern in the food and beverage industry because microorganisms can attach to food-contact surfaces, processing equipment, and other industrial environments despite routine cleaning and sanitation. Once established, biofilms develop an extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) matrix that provides structural stability and protection against mechanical removal, antimicrobial agents, and adverse environmental conditions. Their persistence can facilitate the survival and dissemination of microbial cells and spores, increasing the risk of cross-contamination, foodborne illness, spoilage, reduced shelf life, product recalls, and economic losses. Scope and approach This review provides a comprehensive overview of biofilms in food and beverage processing environments, focusing on mechanisms underlying biofilm formation and persistence, their implications for food safety and product quality, and their industrial significance. It focuses on major pathogenic and spoilage-associated microorganisms that form biofilms, such as Listeria monocytogenes , Salmonella , Escherichia coli , Pseudomonas , Staphylococcus aureus , Bacillus , Geobacillus , and Alicyclobacillus . The review further examines current approaches for biofilm detection and characterization and evaluates emerging anti-biofilm technologies, including ozone, cold plasma, bacteriophages, biosurfactants, nanotechnology, and multi-hurdle strategies. Key findings and conclusions Conventional sanitation may be inadequate against mature biofilms, highlighting the need for integrated monitoring and control. Emerging technologies show potential as alternative or complementary interventions. Key challenges remain in standardizing detection methods, understanding multispecies and…

food.title: Chocolate as a delivery matrix for cocoa polyphenols: Processing, matrix structure and gastrointestinal fate
Cultivation of halophilic archaea in shallow subsurface Martian conditions has implications for extant life on Mars
food.abstract: The present-day Martian surface is generally considered inhospitable to life because of low atmospheric pressure, intense surface radiation, global desiccation, and oxidizing chemistry, which has been increasing since the late Noachian. However, shallow Martian subsurface regions where mineralogy has shown groundwater movement may include localized hypersaline environments capable of retaining liquid water and supporting microbial metabolism. Haloferax volcanii , a model halophilic archaeon, has previously been shown to survive under low-pressure Martian conditions (24 mbar) and to grow anaerobically supported by the Mars-relevant oxyanions nitrate and perchlorate under high-salinity conditions. Here, we investigated whether H. volcanii could actively grow under a combination of environmental and chemical conditions relevant to potentially habitable shallow subsurface Martian lacustrine settings. Cultures were incubated for 160 days under anoxic, CO₂-enriched, low-pressure conditions (24 mbar) in hypersaline liquid media supplemented with nitrate or perchlorate. Growth was observed in all low-pressure treatments and was confirmed by increases in optical density and biological reduction of nitrate and perchlorate. Scanning electron microscopy revealed extensive biofilm formation in low-pressure cultures, and Raman spectroscopy demonstrated the persistence of carotenoid biosignatures after prolonged incubation under Martian conditions. Liquid loss remained below 4% across all treatments, indicating long-term stability of hypersaline brines throughout the experiment. These results demonstrate for the first time that a halophilic archaeon is capable of active growth and metabolism under a Mars-relevant combination of low pressure, high salinity, anoxia, and oxidizing…

food.title: A Recall of Salt-Treated Fermented Canned Anchovies
food.abstract: This study describes the recall of salt-treated fermented canned anchovies (STFCAs) because of elevated histamine levels and bursting cans. STFCAs are a unique food item in that they are salt treated, fermented and canned, but not thermally processed. Thus, the mesophilic bacteria or bacterial spores, including those that can form histamine, are not destroyed by a thermal treatment. STFCAs have a limited shelf life due to a lack of a thermal inactivation step for the halophilic or proteinaceous bacteria, thus at the end of the shelf life the anchovy fillets can turn mushy in the can. Even though the STFCAs are held in an anaerobic environment during fermentation and after canning, and are not thermally treated, they are protected from Clostridium botulinum and Staphylococcus aureus growth and toxin formation by their elevated salt content and low water activity (a w ). The histamine forming bacteria (HFB) growth and sensorial degradation in the STFCAs can be limited with temperature control. We propose STFCAs should be held at or below 10°C (50°F) from manufacturing to consumption. We present calculated No Observed Adverse Effect Level (NOAEL) for STFCAs for the typical United States serving size of 15 g (∼1/2-oz), and discuss our proposed temperature control limit for transportation and storage of STFCAs [< 10°C (50°F)] in light of the lowered defect action level (DAL: 35 ppm) and action level (AL: 200 ppm) for histamine in seafood published by the US Food and Drug Administration in 2024. We suggest including the STFCAs in the regulatory exemption listed in CPG 540.525 ( FDA, 2024 ) for dried fish and fermented fish sauce/paste products that are intended for use only as condiments or as minor flavoring ingredients in other food products.

food.title: Safety evaluation of an extension of use of the food enzyme phospholipase A1 from a genetically modified Aspergillus oryzae strain NZYM‐LJ
food.abstract: strain NZYM-LJ by Novozymes A/S. The safety evaluation of this food enzyme was evaluated previously, and it did not give rise to safety concerns when used in one food manufacturing process. Subsequently, the applicant has requested to extend its use to include three additional processes. In this assessment, EFSA updated the safety evaluation of this food enzyme when used in a total of four food manufacturing processes. The dietary exposure was calculated to be up to 1.020 mg of total organic solids (TOS)/kg body weight (bw) per day in European populations. When combined with the no observed adverse effect level previously reported (957.3 mg TOS/kg bw per day, the highest dose tested), the Panel derived a margin of exposure of at least 939. Based on the revised exposure estimation, the newly derived margin of exposure and the previous evaluation, the Panel concluded that this food enzyme does not give rise to safety concerns under the revised intended conditions of use.

food.title: Elevated ozone reshapes wheat root-associated microbiomes through coordinated plant responses and rhizosphere environmental filtering
food.abstract: Elevated tropospheric ozone (O 3 ) threatens crop productivity, but how O 3 -induced changes in plant responses influence root-associated microbiomes remains unclear. We investigated the responses of microbial communities inhabiting the rhizosphere and root endosphere to elevated O 3 using four cultivars grown under ambient and 1.5-fold ambient O 3 in a field-based free-air O 3 -concentration enrichment (FACE) system. Plant traits, root-released organic carbon (ROC), rhizosphere properties, extracellular enzyme activities, and bacterial and fungal communities were jointly analyzed. Elevated O 3 reduced yield and root biomass, with cultivar-dependent changes in ROC. Elevated O 3 consistently increased rhizosphere pH and altered microbial resource allocation, increasing ecoenzymatic vector length by 4.1% and decreasing vector angle by 4.6%. Bacterial communities showed a stronger response than fungal taxonomic communities, particularly in the rhizosphere. However, variation partitioning indicated that soil properties, especially pH, rather than O 3 treatment alone, provided the strongest independent explanation for bacterial community variation. Fungal communities showed limited taxonomic turnover but exhibited shifts in predicted trophic guilds, including increased pathotroph- and saprotroph-associated groups and decreased symbiotroph-containing guilds under elevated O 3 . These results demonstrate that elevated O 3 reshapes the wheat root-associated microbiome through coordinated changes in plant performance, rhizosphere environmental filtering, and microbial functional strategies, highlighting the importance of plant-mediated processes in regulating belowground responses to atmospheric change. IMPORTANCE Elevated tropospheric O 3 is an increasing threat to crop…

food.title: Safety of Garcinia mangostana L. (mangosteen) peel extract as a novel food pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2015/2283
authors: Novel Foods and Food Allergens (NDA) EFSA Panel on Nutrition
food.abstract: Following a request from the European Commission, the EFSA Panel on Nutrition, Novel Foods and Food Allergens (NDA) was asked to deliver an opinion on Garcinia mangostana L. (mangosteen) peel extract as a novel food (NF) pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2015/2283. The NF is a dried, hydro‐alcoholic extract obtained from the peel (pericarp and skin) of the fruit of the mangosteen tree, G. mangostana L. The applicant intends to market the NF for use in food supplements, at a maximum dose of 200 mg per day. The target population proposed by the applicant is the general adult population. The NF is intended to be marketed as standardised to 44%–52% total xanthones, which includes 26%–34% α‐mangostin and 2%–6% γ‐mangostin. The NF showed no genotoxic potential in the provided genotoxicity studies. However, marked cytotoxicity severely restricted the doses that could be tested. The Panel considers the available data insufficient to rule out genotoxicity concerns of the NF. In the provided subchronic toxicity study with the NF in rats, several findings of concern were noted. Marked increases in alanine aminotransferase and total bilirubin concentrations, indicative of liver toxicity, were already observed at the lowest dose. Increases in urea and blood urea nitrogen concentrations, starting at the mid‐dose, point towards kidney toxicity. The lower body weight gains resulting in lower final body weights in all the groups that received the NF compared to the control groups suggests general toxicity of the NF. The Panel considers that a reference point cannot be derived from this study and that, based on the evidence provided, a safe dose for the NF cannot be established. The Panel concludes that the safety of the NF, G. mangostana L. (mangosteen) peel extract, cannot be established.

food.title: Safety of powdered Xanthobacter sp. SoF1 biomass as a novel food pursuant to regulation (EU) 2015/2283
authors: Novel Foods and Food Allergens (NDA) EFSA Panel on Nutrition
food.abstract: sp. SoF1 biomass as a novel food (NF) pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2015/2283. The NF is a bacterial biomass powder and is proposed to be used as an ingredient in several food categories, targeting the general population. The information provided on the production process, composition, stability and specifications of the NF is sufficient and does not raise safety concerns. Consistent with the modest protein quality of the NF, proteolytic fermentation in the colon gave rise to branched SCFA and ammonia. In the Caco-2 model, colonic fermentation induced a modest increase in epithelial permeability, without evidence of cytotoxicity or reduced cell viability. Based on the data provided, the Panel considers that there are no concerns regarding genotoxicity. In a 90-day oral toxicity study, no adverse effects were observed up to the highest dose tested, 1500 mg/kg body weight (bw) per day. Under the proposed conditions of use, the highest 95th percentile intake estimates of the NF ranged from 0.765 mg/kg bw per day in infants to 7.092 mg/kg bw per day in other children. Taking into account the identity, production process, compositional data and the absence of toxicity in the provided studies, the Panel considers that the resulting margins of exposure (MoE) are sufficient, with the lowest MoE being 212 for other children. The Panel considers that the allergenic potential of the NF is unknown and that cross-reactivity to known allergens cannot be excluded. The Panel concludes that the NF is safe under the proposed conditions of use.

food.title: Evaluation of the mycobiota isolated from “Serrano” and Iberian ham as a potential agent to control ochratoxigenic moulds
food.abstract: Moulds are undesirable food contaminants. During the dry-cured ham ripening, surface moulds often develop beneficial to the final product. However, some species, such as Penicillium nordicum, P . verrucosum , and Aspergillus westerdijkiae , which frequently colonise dry-cured ham, produce mycotoxins, ochratoxin A (OTA). To control this hazard, native microorganisms have been proposed as a strategy. This study assessed the capacity of non-toxigenic indigenous yeasts and moulds to inhibit OTA production by ochratoxigenic moulds isolated from “Serrano” and feed-fed and acorn-fed Iberian hams. Biocontrol agents (BCAs), mainly comprising P. solitum , A . proliferans , and Debaryomyces hansenii , were selected and inoculated into ham agar containing a mixture of three ochratoxigenic P. nordicum strains. Samples for each ham type were incubated for two months under industrial curing conditions, divided into two phases (Maturations 1 and 2), mimicking the whole dry-cured ham ripening. The main difference between the maturation phases was that Maturation 1 had lower temperatures and higher relative humidity than Maturation 2. The highest significant OTA levels were found during Maturation 2 in all ham types, with environmental conditions (mainly temperature and water activity) being a key factor in the mycotoxin production. The BCAs consistently reduced OTA levels during both maturation stages compared with the non-treated control. Isolates obtained from feed-fed Iberian ham showed the highest efficacy, achieving mean OTA reductions of 94% and 91% for moulds and yeasts, respectively. Therefore, BCAs isolated from industry may limit OTA accumulation in feed-fed and acorn-fed Iberian hams.

food.title: Dhaka Street Foods: An Integrated Human-Health Risk Assessment
food.abstract: Street-vended foods represent a critical yet underrecognized pathway of environmental exposure to chemical and microbial hazards in rapidly urbanizing low- and middle-income countries. The present study adopts an integrated human-health framework encompassing chemical contamination and associated toxicological risks, microbiological food-safety hazards, and psychosocial health assessed through perceived stress. A total of 105 composite samples representing 15 commonly consumed food items were collected across seven urban zones. Potentially toxic elements were quantified, human health risks were evaluated using deterministic and Monte Carlo-based probabilistic approaches, and contamination sources were identified using Positive Matrix Factorization (PMF). Mean concentrations of Pb and Cd exceeded Codex safety limits. Deterministic (hazard index, HI = 1.6) and probabilistic (95th percentile HI = 9.6) assessments demonstrated elevated non-carcinogenic risk, while estimated lifetime cancer risks exceeded the U.S. EPA acceptable range. Source apportionment indicated industrial emissions and utensil-related contamination as dominant contributors. Microbiological analysis showed that approximately 60% of samples exceeded safety thresholds, with Escherichia coli detected in 46% of samples. Higher street-food consumption was significantly associated with increased perceived stress levels among consumers; however, causal relationships cannot be established due to the cross-sectional design of the study. These findings identify street foods as a significant vector of environmental exposure to multiple hazards and highlight the need for strengthened regulatory surveillance and targeted interventions within informal urban food systems.

food.title: Survey among official veterinarians on condemnation criteria for broiler carcasses with external lesions and its potential use for computer vision applications
food.abstract: Post-mortem inspection (PMI) of broiler carcasses is essential for food safety and provides insights into animal health, welfare, and meat quality. Despite uniform legislation in Europe, condemnation criteria still vary among Official Veterinarians (OVs) and countries. This study aimed to collect data regarding condemnation criteria among European OVs conducting broiler PMI and to suggest how these could be used in the compliance audits of PMI computer vision systems (CVSs). An online survey was conducted among 155 OVs in 14 European countries. Respondents assessed 11 standardized image sets depicting common external lesions on broiler carcasses across seven severity levels. They were asked to indicate the point at which each lesion should render a carcass unfit for human consumption. A consensus criterion of ≥66% was applied to define a commonly agreed severity level that requires condemnation. Open-ended responses were analyzed to explore factors affecting PMI decisions. High consensus was achieved for clearly visible and advanced lesions, with most benchmarks established at moderate to high severity levels. Greater variability was found for borderline cases, particularly cellulitis and superficial dermatitis. Qualitative analysis of open-ended questions regarding PMI identified three main themes: 1) training needs; 2) lack of harmonization and support in decision-making; 3) OVs’ public health role and implications for broiler health and welfare. The findings emphasized the role of guidelines, experience, and working conditions in condemnation decisions. The collected PMI results may serve as references for harmonized, risk-based PMI and for evaluating CVS performance against OV assessments.
